subject: Evidence delivery format options for SIEM ingest (audit + admin trails)

From: Laura O'Neill <laura.oneill@pineridge-health.com>

Cc: PineRidge Security Ops <security-ops@pineridge-health.com>

Subject: Evidence delivery format options for SIEM ingest (audit + admin trails)

Hi Markus / Vanessa —

We're kicking off SOC 2 fieldwork for PineRidge the first week of September and the auditors have asked for an "export-ready" set of admin/activity logs that we can ingest into our SIEM for sampling. Before we finalize the evidence request, could you confirm the following so we can scope the evidence bundle?

1) What event categories you can export today (admin API calls, console sign-ins, role changes, service principal activity, model deploy/change events, system-level kernel/infra alerts).
2) Default retention for the different categories and whether we can request a historical snapshot (e.g., a 90-day lookback) as a one-off export.
3) Export formats you support for SIEM ingestion (NDJSON, JSONL, Parquet, compressed tarball). Are there field/column schemas you can share?
4) Signed manifest/checksum options for chain-of-custody (SHA256 manifest, zipsigned, or detached signature).
5) Timezone and timestamp fidelity (UTC vs tenant-local, sub-second precision).
6) Any redaction/sample-scrub options we should be aware of for PII prior to handoff.

If convenient, a short example NDJSON sample and a manifest template would be ideal — auditors want to confirm schema mapping and checksum verification before they schedule the ingest. Target timeline: we need the export ready-by 2026-09-01 to align with the first evidence intake window.

(Attachment: request-template.xlsx)

Thanks,
Laura O'Neill
Head of Vendor Assurance
PineRidge Health
laura.oneill@pineridge-health.com

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Laura O'Neill <laura.oneill@pineridge-health.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-13T09:04:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Evidence delivery format options for SIEM ingest (audit + admin trails)

Laura —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up-front, then operational follow-ups below: 

- Event categories: we can export admin API calls, console sign-ins, role/permission changes, model deploy and rollback events, token/credential create/delete events, and operator-run maintenance actions. System infra alerts are exported from infra side and can be included if you want a combined bundle.
- Retention: default admin activity retention is 365 days for tenant-admin events; operator-level debug traces are 90 days. We can produce point-in-time snapshots beyond default retention if requested within 30 days of the window (the snapshot is a timeboxed export with an admin-authorized request).
- Formats: NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON) and gzipped NDJSON are the primary supported outputs for audit logs; parquet is supported for larger bulk exports (columnar) but requires schema mapping.
- Manifests: we provide a signed SHA256 manifest and a detached signature file (PEM). We can also produce a signed tarball on request.
- Timestamps: all logs are recorded in UTC with ms precision.
- Redaction: we support field-level redaction rules at export time (email, ip, user_id) and can additionally provide sampled masked exports for PII-sensitive audits.

Operational next steps (Karthik / Vanessa — can you confirm the export playbook below and I'll get the signed manifest template attached):
- Choose NDJSON vs Parquet (we suggest NDJSON for direct SIEM ingest).
- Confirm window (e.g., 2026-05-01 to 2026-07-31) and sampling (full vs 5% sample).
- Confirm redaction policy (none, field-redact, masked-sample).
- ETA: once confirmed we can produce a signed export within 72 hours (snapshot export + manifest).

I'll attach a small NDJSON example and the manifest template in the next message.

Best,
Markus Klein
Director, Security & Trust
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: redwood-audit-ndjson-sample.ndjson)
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Laura O'Neill <laura.oneill@pineridge-health.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-16T10:33:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Evidence delivery format options for SIEM ingest (audit + admin trails)

Laura —

Adding the more tactical runbook so you can hand to your SIEM team. Karthik and I validated this with infra: 

- Export procedure: runbook id "export-admin-trail-v1" in our internal ops repo — we kick off a snapshot job that pulls per-tenant admin events and writes to S3 staging location encrypted with the customer's KMS key. From there we generate: gzipped NDJSON + signed-manifest.json (SHA256 checksums per file) + detached signature (PEM).
- Checksums: manifest contains per-file SHA256 and a top-level manifest digest. We use RFC 7515-compatible detached signatures for auditor verification.
- Schema: fields included (event_time, event_type, actor_id, actor_type, resource_type, resource_id, change_summary, request_id, region, ip_address). We'll send a full schema CSV.
- Timezone handling: everything in UTC; we include original-local tz if available as event.metadata.local_tz.
- Delivery options: direct S3 transfer to your bucket (cross-account role) or secure HTTPS pull from our temporary signed URL (7 day TTL). For SIEM teams, S3 cross-account is easiest.
- Redaction: we can apply redaction rules at export-time; note that applying redaction will alter checksum validation for raw files — if you require raw + redacted, we can provide both but raw will be encrypted and require additional approvals.

Related links: runbook and schema CSV attached.
(Attachment: signed-manifest-template.json)
(Attachment: runbook-export-steps.md)

If PineRidge wants the S3 cross-account path, we'll need the target bucket ARN and a short-lived cross-account role setup (I can draft the IAM trust policy). Otherwise we'll provide the signed URL bundle.

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Cloud Ops
Redwood Inference

- Redaction: none for the initial handoff; auditors require raw for hashing. We'll sign a non-disclosure amendment if needed.
